statement: Diverse underground organs are morphologically non-equivalent but share functional demands for persistence, regrowth, developmental switching, and tissue remodeling.

statement: The 11-species backbone spans monocot and eudicot representatives and provides an independent BUSCO-based phylogenetic context.
Four candidate modules show broad cross-lineage recurrence across all 11 backbone species, while cell-wall remodeling provides a more restricted but cross-lineage structural component.
The current-scope benchmark recovered expected biological categories linked to meristem/bud regrowth, stress survival, hormone switching, transcriptional regulation, and structural remodeling.

UGO-Omics supports a hypothesis in which underground-organ diversification repeatedly recruits a conserved regeneration-resilience toolkit through module-level convergence and regulatory redeployment.
